title: Trust in Science Is Falling, Global Survey Finds
paragraphs: Trust in science and scientists is falling around the world.
This is according to the 2026 Wellcome Global Monitor report, which is based on survey data from over 140,000 adults living across 140 countries, covering attitudes to science and related issues.
It found that 72% of people today either have "some" or "a lot" of trust in science. While that's still a large majority of people, it's a significant decrease from the 80% who felt the same in 2020.
Over the same time period, the proportion of people who say they trust science "not much" or "not at all" has grown from 13% to 19%.
Scientists themselves are still a well-trusted group, the report's authors say. They are a little behind doctors and nurses in terms of trust, and far ahead of journalists and national governments.

However, levels of trust for scientists are among the most unstable. The percentage of people who trust scientists "a lot" increased from 34% in 2018 to 43% in 2020, but then fell again to 32% in 2025, when the surveys for this report were done.
For comparison, doctors and nurses were trusted "a lot" by 42% in 2018, 45% in 2020 and 39% in 2025 — so while there have been changes, they have not been as large.
"A lot" of trust in governments has stayed at 24% to 26% since 2018, while for journalists, it has stayed close to 18%.

The report also found a link between people's economic circumstances and their trust in science. Those who are finding it hard to get by on their present income are around half as likely to trust science "a lot" compared with people living comfortably — 20% versus 39%.
People who report less trust in their national institutions and governments are also less likely to trust science, as are those living in countries with higher levels of economic inequality.
